title: Great App, just some minor bugs
body:
This is a very intuitive habit tracking app and almost perfect.

Why almost?

1. 
It doesn’t allow me to enter any habit completion track of previous days before the habit was created. ( I wanted to update the data from my previous app history)

2. 
If I tweak the app, previous updated history is invisible on the habit calendar and I can’t update any previous data from the date of tweaked date, which makes me pull my hair. 

Developer: Just address these two points and this app will be perfect habit tracker.
author: AvinashKunchurkar

title: What is this ridiculous pricing?
body: As a person focused on using a good set of tools for being productive, I considered this. I used it for two weeks and thought it’d be a nice to keep it. Then I checked the monthly and yearly price for this thing and oh boy! This is a habit tracking app, charging me as much as a VPN and dedicated computation apps. You know what! I think I’ll permanently move to my under a dollar notebook for habit tracking. Don’t need another app eating up so much for offering basic tracking, and the same advice that I already read in the book

author: Dhariwal R

title: Expensive
body:
This stingy app allows only one habit a time for free-users, making the app less useful. After the free trial is over i have barely used the app. Nobody is gonna open an app to maintain their streak for just one habit. The author knows most of the app users have already bought his book. But still charging high amount for subscription is so lucrative of him. 

James Clear, we thought you could do better. 

Suggestion: introduce something with reward mechanism integrated into the app. For example free extended trails for habit achievers. 

Make this app like bereal or strava - posting pictures after the habit is done. where friends can see and “kudos” their partners.

author: Samyak Nagrale

title: Clearly the best Habit tracker (app) on earth.
body:
Hello, I have been using this app from yesterday after I got to know about it on the Google search app home screen.
I feel grateful for James for creating the app. Because the book inspired and educated me, but I didn’t had the tools to put them into practice earlier.
Also, I have tried some other habit tracking apps, simple ones and complicated ones, a spectrum, but they weren’t close as helpful as this is.
A person who doesn’t knows about James Clear’s Atomic habits or haven’t read or heard him might be skeptic of this app. But once she starts using it, it will be clear why it’s the best. You don’t have to know the concepts in the book. And even if you still want to know, the app has brief contents from the book to help you understand your journey of self-change better.
All the best on your transformation journey!
author: Just Vir

title: Can’t log a habit - Press & hold unresponsive
body: So I realised that the app doesn’t let you log a habit more than once in a day. But what if my habit goal includes doing the micro habit, thrice a day? So even though I can set reminders 3 times to do it, I can’t log all of them. There should be a feature to enable a person to adjust how many times they can log an activity in a habit depending on the reminders they set or some other way

author: dhootrajm

title: Atomic Habits is a way of life
body: The app really focuses on how small incremental yet consistent changes can change your life. It is not a traditional tracking app with a checklist. It is more of a way to help form a habit, and focus on a limited set of habits instead of being all over the place. If you are looking for a reminders/checklist, this is not the app. If you want to learn and implement atomic habits, this app helps tremendously.

title: Amazing initiative
body: James has changed my life in various ways and this app would be an addition to it. I wanted to try this app the day James announced it on his newsletter. I think it is perfect but more things can be added to it later on. The ability not to be able to add more than 1 habit initially and the whole gamified experience is just too good. Also, I am not clear what does it mean when it says “Form More Habits, room for more tiny changes” in the paid version comparison. Will free versions have any limit on the number of habits I can have? Anyways, I am a fan of James work. Thank you so much for this amazing gift to us all.
